reuse.why: The change reuses tag extraction, spreadsheet access, budget writes and undo wrappers, but copyPreviousMonth bypasses the new shared category selector.

duplication.why: Most category selection is consolidated, but copyPreviousMonth duplicates eligibility policy and the new action repeats the income eligibility guard.

placement.why: Budget eligibility and spending calculations remain in budget/actions.ts, with method registration and undo integration in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration, focused tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared selector improves ownership, but maintaining equivalent eligibility rules in its SQL and copyPreviousMonth's conditions leaves avoidable opportunities for drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth independently applies the eligibility policy represented by getFillableCategories.

disguised_duplication.where: getFillableCategories expresses hidden eligibility in SQL and template/fixed exclusions in a filter, while copyPreviousMonth reshapes the same policy into an inline rejection condition.

abstraction_drift.where: getFillableCategories gains includeHiddenCategories and conditional SQL for hidden filtering, while copyPreviousMonth continues applying the policy independently.
